why: The peer range now accepts AI SDK v7, which older agents versions reject with a peer-dependency conflict; the `onChatMessage` callback type also changed.
Stored HTTP session IDs from older versions are now discarded and the client reconnects, and `createMcpHandler` gains SDK v2 support.
Expired Browser Run sessions are now recycled after an HTTP 410 instead of erroring.
The exact-pinned MCP peer dependencies moved from the beta to stable 2.0.0, so installs pinned to the old beta conflict.
Fixes AI SDK v7 telemetry that was missing token counts, finish reasons and tool results.
`WebSocketChatTransport` is newly exported from the framework-neutral entry, which older versions don't provide.
`agentTool` now takes AI SDK flexible schemas, so custom schemas that don't type-check as `FlexibleSchema` now fail type-checking.
Large base64 values returned outside the canonical screenshot shape are now redacted, and TanStack screenshot output is reduced to a summary.
`Agent.runWorkflow()` now passes Workflow `retention` through; older versions ignore it at runtime.
New `buildAgentPath()` and `buildAgentUrl()` helpers don't exist in older versions, so importing them fails.
Request bodies are streamed to sub-agents, so an unread upload is now cancelled instead of being drained by the parent.
Extraction schemas must now be sent as `response_format.json_schema`, so callers using the old field name need to rename it.
Observer error frames are now terminal and no longer rendered as assistant messages.
Toolchain and dependency updates, plus new-project templates, with no change to the API.
`createAISDKTelemetry()` was removed in favor of `wrapAISDK()`.
BrowserConnector now validates tool arguments and rejects JSON-stringified extraction schemas and wrong `cdp.send` session values.
Streamed text segments around tool calls are now joined with spacing, which changes output text.
Chat recovery now always runs, and `chatRecovery: false` silently gets the default configuration.
The `static options.hibernate` switch and in-memory connection mode were removed, so WebSockets always use hibernation.
`useAgentChat` now throttles UI updates at 50ms by default, where it previously rendered every chunk.
Scheduled callbacks now receive the parsed `Schedule` object as their second argument instead of the raw storage row with a string payload.
The published `agents` CLI binary was removed, so invoking it now fails instead of printing a placeholder message and exiting 0.
Changes the `MCPClientManager` lifecycle capability, which is part of the experimental `agents/lifecycle` surface, and keeps the Agent MCP APIs intact.
Routes async callable and streaming responses to the facet WebSocket frame that originated the RPC, which fixes misrouted responses.
SDK-created spans now carry extra instrumentation and agent identity attributes.
Fixes a false error on long stream resumes by batching replayed chunks.
Corrects compaction overlay scoping and ordering to match intended branch behavior.
Fixes sub-agent WebSocket routing, ordering and error reporting.
Turns an Agent initialization failure on older runtimes into working behavior.
subAgent(), abortSubAgent(), deleteSubAgent(), hasSubAgent() and listSubAgents() are now @deprecated but still work, with this.dynamicAgents as the new surface.
The pull-based alarm contribution model is removed (getNextAlarm/onAlarm on capabilities, LifecycleServices.alarms, AlarmContribution), so code using it fails.
Adds RoutedAgents in the new agents/routing entry point, which older versions lack.
The agents/experimental/memory/session and utils subpaths are removed (Session.create, SessionManager, Postgres providers), with replacements in agents/sessions and agents/context.
cleanupStreamBuffers and STREAM_CLEANUP_DELAY_SECONDS are removed from agents/chat.
Removes the memory-limit policy hooks (applyMemoryLimitPolicy, setLifecycleAlarmMemoryLimitStrikes, _cf_recoveryAlarmCallbacks), which fail for code that used them.
Adds the agents/voice and agents/channels subpath exports, which older versions reject.
WebSocket support moves out of Lifecycle into the WebSockets capability, so Lifecycle's getConnections/getConnection/broadcast and its WebSocket hooks are gone.
Defines dispatch semantics for the job queue introduced in this same release, so there is no prior released behavior.
The tool result sent to the model no longer includes the durable calls log.
Moves chat recovery onto Tasks internally while preserving existing recovery behavior.
Replatforms chat streams onto Streams with automatic migration and an unchanged wire protocol.
Fixes compaction summaries rendering structured tool outputs as [object Object].
Storage write-count optimizations on tables that were never released.
Adds the experimental agents/streams entry point.
Changes only the experimental Sessions capability.
Fixes sub-agent connection state set in onConnect being lost for the first client message.
The default chat recovery work budget changes from 1000 to 10000, with the unit now a durable segment.
Changes only the experimental Sessions capability.
Adds the experimental agents/tasks capability and experimental this.tasks.
Adds a transport option to useAgent and AgentClient, which older versions reject as a type error, and removes the experimental capnweb endpoint.
Queued callbacks now run from the alarm loop and no longer see the enqueuing request's connection via getCurrentAgent(), and dequeue/getQueue methods became async.
State moves into a capability while Agent's public API and wire protocol are stated to be unchanged.
Protocol state sync and connection flags move into WebSockets, with Agent's public methods and wire behaviour unchanged.
The `{ fallback: true }` option and LifecycleUseOptions are removed in favor of a `claims` declaration.
Preserves the fiber body's result when bookkeeping cleanup fails, instead of replacing it with a cleanup error.
Adds a new property; older versions simply lack it, and the finalizePending change is a minor retry fix.
Dependency bump of valibot for a security advisory with no API change.
Async RPC on Agents addressed by raw IDs from newUniqueId()/idFromString() now fails the first call.
Corrects a failed agent-tool child being reported incorrectly after eviction.
Fixes duplicated or dropped agent-tool chunks on reconnect and recovery.
Adds the `eventDelivery: "terminal"` option to runAgentTool; older versions ignore the unknown option.
New experimental entry point agents/models/ai-sdk.
New experimental entry point agents/models/pi-ai.
New experimental entry point agents/harnesses/pi.
Fixes input being lost when approval arrives before input finishes streaming.
loadCdpSpec gains an optional sessionId argument; older versions ignore it.
Turns an unclear failure into a clear BrowserRenderingError when no WebSocket is returned.
CdpConnection is the new name and CdpSession is kept as a deprecated alias.
Persistent browser tools are backed by experimental Browser sessions.
send() now rejects promptly on a closed socket instead of waiting for the timeout.
cdp.spec() and loadCdpSpec() return richer output including parameters, return types, and type details.
useAgentChat now loads the new agent's history when the address changes, as expected.
useAgentChat gains an onTurnEnd callback, and terminal chat frames now carry outcomes and user message IDs.
A WebSocket close before the done frame now sets error state instead of showing a truncated answer as complete.
Compaction summaries echoed back by clients are no longer stored, and stored duplicates are hidden.
New context block option value that older versions don't recognize, and code not using it is unaffected.
Broadcasts from sub-agents now make at most one root call and none without recipients, changing observable calls with the same code.
Fixes a failure of a facet's first call after restart caused by syncing root-owned jobs, turning an error into working behavior.
Fixes WebSocket connections to deeply nested sub-agents that failed, making them work as documented.
The hook now replaces a scrambled assistant message with the server snapshot instead of keeping it until reload.
onToolCall now fires only after the stream ends and only for tool calls still waiting on the client, so timing and call set change.
Interfaces are newly accepted as Props, which older versions rejected with a type error.
resolveToolMergeId is deprecated in favour of reconcileMessages and still works.
ready now resolves only after state arrives, so code that ran at ready sees state defined instead of undefined.
Stops reconnecting from erasing messages sent while disconnected, which is the expected behavior.
Corrects the documented default and unit only, with no behavior change.
Clients stop reconnecting after sub-agent rejection and terminal rejections use new close codes, changing observable close codes and reconnect behavior.
Fixes duplicated text on reconnect during a tool continuation.
onChatResponse now fires with recovered: true for turns persisted just before a Durable Object reset, where it previously did not fire.
Stops onFiberRecovered from being called for already finished work, which is the documented behavior.
New method that older versions lack and that only adds a call.
Fixes attachment references being lost so media is garbage-collected when a message is written back.
Performance optimization that reduces reads with no observable output change.
Approved tool calls that never ran are now settled so later turns no longer send them unresolved, changing what is sent to the model.
Fixes thread locking, queued follow-up retention and typing ordering during slow delivery.
Fixes recovery of an interrupted regeneration so it lands on its own branch.
Fixes a thrown 'Maximum update depth exceeded' error during long streams.
With storeTools: true, oversized tool payloads are now recorded with base64 summarized rather than dropped.
Vague hardening of recovery without saying what observably changes.
deleteSubAgent now also closes the sub-agent's direct client connections, a new side effect for the same call.
Corrects invalid tool outputs after truncation (issue #2014), turning broken results into working ones.
Makes withX402Client enforce maxPaymentValue on the requirement actually signed, as the option already promises.
Dependency bump of pi-durable and pi-ai with no stated user-visible change.
New experimental harnesses only.
New agents/websearch entry point with a web_search tool; older versions cannot resolve the import.
The old agents/channels entry point was removed, so imports from it now fail.
Summary list of bug fixes across several features.
AiSdkHarness is one of the new experimental harnesses.
Adds Channels to the experimental channels entry point.
Breaking removal of the agents/channels entry points, ChannelHost, composites and helpers; imports now fail.
ChannelGateway is added only under agents/experimental/channels.
WebChannelChatTransport lives under the experimental channels entry point.
Web Channel and its client are new experimental entry points.
New agents/websearch entry point providing a web_search tool; older versions reject the import.
Change only to the experimental AiSdkHarness.
Fix only to the experimental AiSdkHarness.
Change only to the experimental AiSdkHarness.
browserTool now sends its own tool description to the model, changing how the model uses it.
The tui command is a client for the experimental Web Channel.
New experimental container harness entry points.
removeServer() and removeMcpServer() now also delete the server's saved OAuth state from storage.
New experimental OpenCode harness and model entry points.
Fixes live Streams readers stalling when chunks arrive during processing.
Fixes a 'no such table' error when two Streams instances share an object.
Turns a thrown 'Invalid job outcome' alarm error into a quiet end.
ThinkHarness is a new export from the experimental agents/harness/think entry point.
For URLs behind Cloudflare Access, the CLI now fetches a cloudflared token and sends it on the WebSocket upgrade, which it did not do before.
A URL with a #fragment used to make the client exit before connecting and now works.
After a mid-stream WebSocket drop, a cut-off assistant reply is now replaced with the server's copy, so the resulting message state differs.
send() and listConversations() on a closed client now reject instead of hanging forever, and follow()/close() cancel pending reconnects, so code relying on the old behavior now sees errors.
paidTool now works with MCP SDK v2 servers and matches payment headers case-insensitively, turning a failure into working behavior.
